identity.name: CONTINENTAL PETROLEUMS LTD.
identity.industry: Industrial Lubricants & Hazardous Waste Incineration / Power EPC

summary.oneLiner: Continental Petroleums delivered 112% YoY revenue growth in FY25 driven by EPC order wins and premium lubricant sales, with EBITDA margin expanding to 34.3%; the key shift is from low-margin bulk sales to high-margin specialty products and scalable EPC execution, positioning the company for sustained growth in regulated industrial segments.

one-line thesis: Continental Petroleums delivered 112% YoY revenue growth in FY25 driven by EPC order wins and premium lubricant sales, with EBITDA margin expanding to 34.3%; the key shift is from low-margin bulk sales to high-margin specialty products and scalable EPC execution, positioning the company for sustained growth in regulated industrial segments.
financial scorecard: revenue: 113 Cr (+112% YoY); EBITDA: 8 Cr (34.3% margin); PAT (reported): 4.3 Cr (+57.9% YoY); PAT (normalized): 4.3 Cr (no major one-offs); order book: 240 Cr (EPC); net debt: increased short-term borrowings to fund EPC execution, long-term debt reduced
guidance: revenue growth: 20-25% YoY (FY26); margin: lubricants to reach 12-15% gross (from 10-12%); order inflow: targeting 260-270 Cr in new EPC bids; capex/commissioning: Co-processing unit (6-7 months to commission), lubricant automation, solar EPC equipment
order book & pipeline: 240 Cr in EPC projects (12-18 month execution horizon); additional 268 Cr bids submitted, expected to be awarded in next 1-2 months
segment / subsidiary detail: Lubricants: 50-55% of revenue, 10-12% gross margin, shifting to branded Contol and specialty greases; Incineration: 20-25% of revenue, high compliance-driven demand; EPC: 25-30% of revenue, 30-35% EBITDA margin, project-based
growth verticals / optionality: Co-processing unit (new waste stream monetization), expansion into Chittorgarh/Bhilwara for incineration, OEM partnerships for lubricants, solar EPC equipment integration
margins & cost dynamics: Lubricants: gross margin expanding from 10-12% to 12-15% via premium products; EPC: margins sustained via lean execution; incineration: stable margins due to regulatory moat; cost pressure from raw material volatility mitigated by automation
capex / expansion: FY26 CapEx focused on: (1) Co-processing unit (incineration) - ₹40-50 Cr; (2) Lubricant packaging automation - ₹15-20 Cr; (3) Solar EPC equipment - ₹10 Cr; total estimated ₹65-85 Cr, ROI-driven
capital allocation: Deleveraging (reduced LT debt), funding EPC project execution via ST borrowings, CapEx prioritized for incineration expansion and automation; no dilution planned; dividends not mentioned
risks & watch-items: EPC project execution delays (government approvals), regulatory changes in hazardous waste, raw material price volatility (base oils), competition in lubricants from multinational brands
management quality / tone: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized operational discipline, margin expansion, and regulatory tailwinds; acknowledged need for better cost control in EPC; committed to transparency and segment-wise disclosures going forward
non-obvious takeaways: Incineration unit's ash output is not waste but a regulated byproduct with potential for future reuse (e.g., construction aggregate), creating latent asset value; Co-processing unit allows burning lower-calorific waste, expanding addressable market beyond current 3000+ kcal/kg feedstock
